title: Finite constraints and infinite choices: Rado's lemma and distinct representatives

based_on.title: Hall's marriage theorem
based_on.venue: Journal of the London Mathematical Society (2)

summary: Finite available choices let solutions to every finite selection problem assemble into one global solution.
abstract: Suppose we want to choose one element from each of many sets, with no repeated choices. A necessary condition is that every finite collection of these sets contains at least as many available elements as there are sets in that collection. Assuming choice, Hall’s theorem makes this an exact criterion, even for an infinite family, provided each individual set is finite. A single infinite set of possibilities can make every finite test pass while preventing distinct choices for the whole family.
